label: copy-phase input q (re-fed q)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the input is the letter q. That q is the model reading its own earlier q output back in. It never fires during the original phase (including on q there), at <DEL>, or on any other input token; there is 1 stray dev activation on g. Activation grows with position: it is weak at recall_idx 1 (right after <DEL>, mean around 0.1-0.3 of max) and strongest late in long sequences (top examples near 1.0 when q is re-fed around recall_idx 7). The false positives (about 10% of predicted steps) are copy-phase q inputs at early absolute steps (t <= 7) in short sequences (L = 3-5). Magnitude does not depend much on which token is being output.

issues: Core claims check out. Every one of the 81,684 dev activations is in the copy phase, with 0 in the original phase and 0 at <DEL>. 81,683 of them have q as input, plus 1 stray on g. Test recall is 1.0 and test misses show 0 missed activations.

The false positives are a known, already-disclosed class rather than an unexplained one: precision is 0.29 when L<=4, 0.53 when t<=7, and 0.98 when t>=8. Test misses show mostly short sequences (L=3-4).

Small inaccuracy: the weakness is driven by absolute step t and length L, not by recall_idx. With recall_idx==1 and t>=8, precision is 0.95 (it is 0.73 for recall_idx==1 overall). For example, the test false positive 'q r c u 3 x 1 c 1 <DEL> *q*' is recall_idx 1 at t=10, so it is an exception to the stated t<=7 pattern.
Adding L>=5 to the predicate raises test F1 from 0.947 to 0.964 (precision 0.957, recall 0.970). This is a minor improvement, not evidence of a missing mechanism.
